human_interaction_patterns.notes: User can update cart multiple times before moving to checkout. Recommend Update with validation to ensure cart data structure is valid. Update handler should accept cart status and items, validate them, and store in workflow instance variables.

complexity_factors: 4 levels of nesting (DO_WHILE > SWITCH > nested SWITCH with cases)
DO_WHILE loop with multiple WAIT tasks requiring human interaction
Multiple SWITCH statements with nested control flow
Two WAIT tasks expecting external data at different loop stages
Complex state management with multiple SET_VARIABLE tasks updating shared state

recommended_patterns.human_interaction: Updates recommended for 2 WAIT tasks (cart_wait_ref and checkout_wait_ref). Both should validate incoming data structure. cart_wait should validate cart status and items format. checkout_wait should validate success status values.
recommended_patterns.error_handling: No explicit retry policies in Conductor tasks. Recommend adding RetryPolicy for SUB_WORKFLOW execution (checkout_task) to handle transient failures during checkout processing.
recommended_patterns.parallel_execution: No parallel execution in this workflow - all tasks are sequential or conditional
recommended_patterns.loop_handling: DO_WHILE loop requires careful implementation. Since loop depends on external signals, consider: (1) Adding timeout to wait_condition calls, (2) Implementing continue-as-new if user could make many cart updates, (3) Adding query handler to check current cart state
special_considerations: Two different WAIT tasks in workflow create complex signal/update handling - need two separate update handlers with different data structures
Loop condition checks workflow.variables.cart == 'checkout', which is set by external signal - ensure signal handler updates this correctly
SUB_WORKFLOW 'pi_calc_test' must be migrated separately before this workflow can be fully tested
INLINE task with JavaScript expression '({ someKey: 'someValue' })' - straightforward translation to Python dict literal
Nested SWITCH within SWITCH creates deep conditional logic - consider refactoring into helper methods for readability
Workflow has no explicit timeout (timeoutSeconds: 0) - consider adding execution_timeout when starting workflow to prevent indefinite waiting

translation_notes: This workflow implements a shopping cart state machine with user interaction at multiple stages
Main loop continues until cart status changes to 'checkout' via external signal
Two critical external interaction points: (1) cart updates during shopping, (2) checkout success confirmation
The workflow has no activities (SIMPLE or HTTP tasks) - all logic is control flow and variable manipulation
Consider implementing workflow queries to allow external systems to check current cart state without sending signals
The defaultCase in shopping_checkout_ref executes INLINE JavaScript - this runs when cart status is not 'checkout' (i.e., during shopping phase)
The checkout case has sequential execution: SUB_WORKFLOW -> WAIT -> nested SWITCH, all must complete before loop continues
If checkout fails (checkout_failed case), cart resets to 'shopping' and loop continues, allowing user to modify cart and retry
If checkout succeeds (default case in nested switch), cart_items is cleared and cart remains 'checkout', exiting the loop
Manual testing will require: (1) Sending cart updates via Update handler, (2) Sending checkout confirmation via different Update handler, (3) Testing both success and failure paths
